answer: Because the atlas stake is held until the river settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the cedar audit lists each exposure. A farm running 28 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. An attester must stake 17% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. That is 35 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
